subject: Finishes that connect living spaces
hook: Open-plan rooms feel calmer when the finishes repeat on purpose.
ig:
Open-plan rooms feel calmer when the finishes repeat on purpose.

If your kitchen, dining and living areas share one space, the furniture needs to read as one family. Our five rules:

Lead finish. The biggest surface, usually kitchen doors, sets the tone.

One accent. Oak-effect next to charcoal or matt white adds warmth. Stop at two finishes plus your worktop.

Repeat three times. An accent seen once looks like an afterthought. Carry it into a sideboard, shelving or alcove units.

Handles as the link. The same antique gold or matt black across kitchen and living furniture connects rooms more than people expect.

Test against the floor. It's the one thing every zone shares, so samples go down on it in daylight.

Because our furniture is made to measure, the living-room pieces can be built in the same finishes as the kitchen, rather than hunting for a near match.

Save this for your plans and tap the link in bio to see what we make.
fb:
Open-plan living is lovely until the kitchen, dining table and TV unit all look like they came from different houses.

The fix is simpler than you'd think: one lead finish, one accent, repeat the accent a few times, keep the handles consistent, and check everything against your floor in daylight.

As everything we make is built to measure in our Hanley workshop, your living-room units can be made in the same finishes as your kitchen. Have a look at what we make.

on_asset:
S1: Make open-plan rooms feel like one / Five finish rules that link spaces |
S2: Pick one lead finish — Choose the finish that covers the most surface, often the kitchen doors, and let it set the tone for the furniture around it. |
S3: Add one accent, not four — A second finish, such as oak-effect against charcoal, adds warmth. A third or fourth starts to look accidental. |
S4: Repeat it three times — An accent used once looks like a mistake. Echo it in the shelves, a sideboard and an alcove unit. |
S5: Use handles as the thread — Antique gold or matt black on the kitchen, then the same on the media unit and sideboard, ties rooms together quietly. |
S6: Check against the floor — Your flooring runs through every zone. Hold samples against it in daylight before deciding anything. |
S7: Lead, accent, repeat, handles, floor — Save this, then bring your flooring photo to a free design consultation. Link in bio.
